callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

The CI ratchet failure is definitively: `NEW > 8 js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12`.

CRAP=12 with what CC and cov? The report line for isPrBodyFrozen isn't in top 30 (CRAP 12 too low). Let me estimate: isPrBodyFrozen has CC: base 1 + if(!pr||typeof!==object) [1+1] + if(merged) [1] + if(state=='closed'||state=='merged') [1+1] + for [1] + if(indexOf!==-1) [1] = 9. CRAP=12 = CC²·(1-cov)²·0.5 + CC → 40.5·(1-cov)² = 3 → (1-cov)² = 0.074 → cov ≈ 0.73. So coverage ≈73% (11 of 15 branches/lines?). If full coverage, CRAP = 9 ≤ 8? No — 9 > 8! Even at 100% coverage, CC=9 → CRAP=9 > threshold 8 → still fails!

Let me verify CC counting. crap4js uses cyclomatic complexity ( decision points + 1):
- function base: 1
- `if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object')` → +2 (two conditions)
- `if (pr.merged === true)` → +1
- `if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged')` → +2
- `for` loop → +1
- ternary `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? ... : ...` → +2
- `if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1)` → +1
Total CC = 1+2+1+2+1+2+1 = 10? Then CRAP at cov=1 → 10. With cov≈0.9: 100·0.01·0.5+10 = 10.5. Hmm CI says 12.

Anyway — the key finding: **isPrBodyFrozen as written exceeds the CRAP threshold of 8 and CI fails**. This is a BLOCKING issue (red CI). The rework must either reduce complexity (simplify the function) or add coverage... no wait, if CC ≥ 9, full coverage still gives CRAP ≥ 9 > 8. So the function must be simplified to CC ≤ 8, or split.

Actually let me compute what CC gives 12 at some coverage. If CC=8: 32(1-cov)²+8=12 → cov=0.646. If CC=9: cov≈0.728. If CC=10: 50(1-cov)²+10=12 → cov≈0.8. Any case, even perfect coverage likely ≥9 → still fails if CC≥9. If CC=8 with 100% coverage → CRAP=8, not >8 → passes. So it depends on exact CC count. The safest rework: simplify the function so CC ≤ 8 even counting all branches.

Simplest simplification: 
```js
function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
   if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
   if (pr.merged === true) return true;
   var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
   if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged') return true;
   return labelNames(pr.labels).some(...);
}
```
Still similar. Extract label normalization to a helper `labelName(label)` and use a loop... Extracting the label-scan into its own function reduces isPrBodyFrozen's CC: 1 + 2 (||) + 1 + 2 (||) + 1 (call if?) = 7 if written as:

```js
function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
   if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
   if (pr.merged === true) return true;
   var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
   if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged') return true;
   return hasMergeQueueLabel(pr.labels);
}
```
CC = 1+2+1+2+1 = 7 (the `return hasMergeQueueLabel` adds nothing). With full coverage CRAP=7 ≤ 8 → passes. The helper `hasMergeQueueLabel` would itself be new: 1 + for(1) + ternary(2) + if(1) = 5 ≤ 8 → fine.

Alternatively use Array.prototype.some — but the codebase... they use ES5-style for loops. Actually `.some` would reduce: 
```js
return (pr.labels || []).some(function(l) { return MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(...) !== -1; });
```
CC = 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1(some) + 1(callback if)... hmm nested functions counted separately. 

OK, so the review: BLOCKING finding = CI failure with root cause identified: `isPrBodyFrozen` CC too high (CRAP 12 > 8). Suggest extracting the label scan.

Now, other review findings. Let me look at correctness issues:

1. **Findings verification — does the fix actually address gh-960?** The ticket: PR body must be final before merge queue; finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms. The fix freezes body rewrite when `ai_validating` label present OR merged/closed. But wait — the live incident: PR #956 merged with Closes added at merge moment. In that lifecycle, the rework leg died; a later run finalized. Where does the finalize-step rewrite happen? Does the finalize step also call `postReworkBodyAndComment`? The freeze is only in `postTestReworkResults.js` — the rework publish path. The ticket says "the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms". Is there another body-rewrite path (finalize step) that still rewrites the body post-arm? E.g., `machineMerge` or `retryMerge` or developTicketAndCreatePR finalize. Let me grep for updatePrBody / updatePullRequestBody callers.

2. **`pr.merged` shape**: github_list_prs — does the PR object include `merged` and `labels`? The GitHub REST list PRs API returns `merged` (wait — list PRs does NOT return `merged` field! GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls returns: url, id, number, state, locked, title, user, body, labels, milestone, active_lock_reason, created_at, closed_at, merged_at, merge_commit_sha, assignee, ... It does NOT include `merged`. `merged` is only on the single-PR GET response. However state='closed' covers merged PRs anyway. And listPrs('open') means closed never returned. So `pr.merged === true` check is harmless defense.

But important: does the GitHub SCM's github_list_prs return labels? Need to check the dmtools catalog — github_list_prs presumably returns the REST JSON array with labels as [{name}]. Probably yes.

Also GitLab MRs: _normalizeGitLabMr — what labels does it produce? GitLab doesn't have labels on MRs in the same way... Actually GitLab 15.x+ supports MR labels. Let me check _normalizeGitLabMr.

3. **The real gate**: freeze on `ai_validating` label. In the live incident, did the PR have `ai_validating` at the time of the finalize rewrite? The PR #956 merged 10:55Z; the rewrite happened at merge time when the merge bot had armed validation. The finalize body rewrite happened after validation armed → label present → frozen. Good. But there's a subtlety: `postTestReworkBodyAndComment` is the rework-publish path. In the incident, a later run "finalized" — was that a rework run? ticket says rework leg died on push, later run finalized. So the finalizing run was presumably a test-rework resume that published results and rewrote body at 10:55. With the freeze, when it re-runs post-arm, body rewrite is skipped. 

But wait — there's a subtle failure mode: `findTestPRForTicket` uses `scm.listPrs('open')`. Fine.

4. **Ordering in updatePullRequestBody**: `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` — ensures Closes line is FIRST in the body. But the refreshed body replaces the entire PR body with `## ticketKey Result ... + bodyContent`. If bodyContent (outputs/pr_body.md) doesn't include the original PR description, this was already the pre-existing behavior. Fine.

One issue: previously the body had whatever content; now Closes is force-prepended — that changes body structure but is intended.

5. Idempotency check in ensureClosesLine: regex `\bCloses\s+#?952\b` case-insensitive — if bodyContent already contains "Closes #952" it's left as-is (possibly not first). Test asserts first when not present. OK.

6. **`pr.number` used in warn when pr could be null**: `postReworkBodyAndComment` — if pr is null, `pr && pr.number` → 'undefined' — fine, but then `scm.addComment(pr.number...)` would throw — but that's inside try. Pre-existing.

7. Edge: `isPrBodyFrozen` — what if `pr` object comes from GitLab normalized MR — state 'merged' vs 'opened'. _normalizeGitLabMr probably maps state. If GitLab MR state normalized to 'open'/'closed'... merged MRs have merged_at. In listPrs('open') only open returned. Fine.

8. Duplication: The label-freeze concept — does something similar exist elsewhere (e.g., a `hasLabel` helper)? grep for existing helpers to avoid duplication.

Let me also check other body-rewrite paths for the "finalize step" per the ticket. The ticket AC: "the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms". # gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.

    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

Anyway — the key finding: **isPrBodyFrozen as written exceeds the CRAP threshold of 8 and CI fails**. This is a BLOCKING issue (red CI). The rework must either reduce complexity (simplify the function) or add coverage... no wait, if CC ≥ 9, full coverage still gives CRAP ≥ 9 > 8. So the function must be simplified to CC ≤ 8, or split.

Actually let me compute what CC gives 12 at some coverage. If CC=8: 32(1-cov)²+8=12 → cov=0.646. If CC=9: cov≈0.728. If CC=10: 50(1-cov)²+10=12 → cov≈0.8. Any case, even perfect coverage likely ≥9 → still fails if CC≥9. If CC=8 with 100% coverage → CRAP=8, not >8 → passes. So it depends on exact CC count. Simplest simplification:

function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {

```

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

CRAP=12 = CC²·(1-cov)²·0.5 + CC → 40.5·(1-cov)² = 3 → (1-cov)² = 0.074 → cov ≈ 0.73. So coverage ≈73% (11 of 15 branches/lines?). If full coverage, CRAP = 9 ≤ 8? No — 9 > 8! Even at 100% coverage, CC=9 → CRAP=9 > threshold 8 → still fails!

Let me verify CC counting. crap4js uses cyclomatic complexity ( decision points + 1):
- function base: 1
- `if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object')` → +2 (two conditions)
- `if (pr.merged === true)` → +1
- `if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged')` → +2

Total CC = 1+2+1+2+1+2+1 = 10? Then CRAP at cov=1 → 10. With cov≈0.9: 100·0.01·0.5+10 = 10.5. Hmm CI says 12.

Anyway — the key finding: **isPrBodyFrozen as written exceeds the CRAP threshold of 8 and CI fails**. This is a BLOCKING issue (red CI). The rework must either reduce complexity (simplify the function) or add coverage... no wait, if CC ≥ 9, full coverage still gives CRAP ≥ 9 > 8. So the function must be simplified to CC ≤ 8, or split.

Actually let me compute what CC gives 12 at some coverage. If CC=8: 32(1-cov)²+8=12 → cov=0.646. If CC=9: cov≈0.728. If CC=10: 50(1-cov)²+10=12 → cov≈0.8. Any case, even perfect coverage likely ≥9 → still fails if CC≥9. If CC=8 with 100% coverage → CRAP=8, not >8 → passes. So it depends on exact CC count. The safest rework: simplify the function so CC ≤ 8 even counting all branches.

Simplest simplification: 
```js
function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
   if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
   if (pr.merged === true) return true;
   var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
   if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged') return true;

```
Still similar. Extract label normalization to a helper `labelName(label)` and use a loop... Extracting the label-scan into its own function reduces isPrBodyFrozen's CC: 1 + 2 (||) + 1 + 2 (||) + 1 (call if?) = 7 if written as:

```js
function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
   if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
   if (pr.merged === true) return true;
   var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();

CC = 1+2+1+2+1 = 7 (the `return hasMergeQueueLabel` adds nothing). With full coverage CRAP=7 ≤ 8 → passes. The helper `hasMergeQueueLabel` would itself be new: 1 + for(1) + ternary(2) + if(1) = 5 ≤ 8 → fine.

return (pr.labels || []).some(function(l) { return MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(...) !== -1; });
```
CC = 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1(some) + 1(callback if)... hmm nested functions counted separately.

1. **Findings verification — does the fix actually address gh-960?** The ticket: PR body must be final before merge queue; finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms. The fix freezes body rewrite when `ai_validating` label present OR merged/closed. But wait — the live incident: PR #956 merged with Closes added at merge moment. GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls returns: url, id, number, state, locked, title, user, body, labels, milestone, active_lock_reason, created_at, closed_at, merged_at, merge_commit_sha, assignee, ... It does NOT include `merged`. `merged` is only on the single-PR GET response. However state='closed' covers merged PRs anyway. And listPrs('open') means closed never returned. So `pr.merged === true` check is harmless defense.

But important: does the GitHub SCM's github_list_prs return labels? Need to check the dmtools catalog — github_list_prs presumably returns the REST JSON array with labels as [{name}]. Probably yes.

# gh-960: PR body 'Closes #N' lands at merge time → GitHub auto-close never fires (live #956/#952)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17: PR #956 (fix for #952) merged 10:55Z with `Closes #952` as the first body line, but #952 stayed OPEN. Evidence: #952's timeline has only `referenced` events — no `cross-referenced` (the event GitHub creates when a closing keyword is parsed); #956's body updatedAt == mergedAt (10:55Z). Conclusion: the closing keyword was added to the body at/after the merge moment (finalize-step body rewrite), so GitHub never parsed it — closing keywords are evaluated on PR creation and body edits, and post-merge edits are too late. All six CRAP PRs the same morning auto-closed their issues normally — #956's lifecycle was atypical (rework leg died on push at 10:23Z, a later run finalized). Fix: the PR body (including the Closes keyword) must be final BEFORE the PR enters the merge queue; the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

blocks.text:
The CI ratchet failure is definitively: `NEW > 8 js/common/pullRequest.js::isPrBodyFrozen: 12`.

CRAP=12 with what CC and cov? The report line for isPrBodyFrozen isn't in top 30 (CRAP 12 too low). Let me estimate: isPrBodyFrozen has CC: base 1 + if(!pr||typeof!==object) [1+1] + if(merged) [1] + if(state=='closed'||state=='merged') [1+1] + for [1] + if(indexOf!==-1) [1] = 9. CRAP=12 = CC²·(1-cov)²·0.5 + CC → 40.5·(1-cov)² = 3 → (1-cov)² = 0.074 → cov ≈ 0.73. So coverage ≈73% (11 of 15 branches/lines?). If full coverage, CRAP = 9 ≤ 8? No — 9 > 8! Even at 100% coverage, CC=9 → CRAP=9 > threshold 8 → still fails!

Let me verify CC counting. crap4js uses cyclomatic complexity ( decision points + 1):
- function base: 1
- `if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object')` → +2 (two conditions)
- `if (pr.merged === true)` → +1
- `if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged')` → +2
- `for` loop → +1
- ternary `labels[i] && labels[i].name !== undefined ? ... : ...` → +2
- `if (MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(String(name)) !== -1)` → +1
Total CC = 1+2+1+2+1+2+1 = 10? Then CRAP at cov=1 → 10. With cov≈0.9: 100·0.01·0.5+10 = 10.5. Hmm CI says 12.

Anyway — the key finding: **isPrBodyFrozen as written exceeds the CRAP threshold of 8 and CI fails**. This is a BLOCKING issue (red CI). The rework must either reduce complexity (simplify the function) or add coverage... no wait, if CC ≥ 9, full coverage still gives CRAP ≥ 9 > 8. So the function must be simplified to CC ≤ 8, or split.

Actually let me compute what CC gives 12 at some coverage. If CC=8: 32(1-cov)²+8=12 → cov=0.646. If CC=9: cov≈0.728. If CC=10: 50(1-cov)²+10=12 → cov≈0.8. Any case, even perfect coverage likely ≥9 → still fails if CC≥9. If CC=8 with 100% coverage → CRAP=8, not >8 → passes. So it depends on exact CC count. The safest rework: simplify the function so CC ≤ 8 even counting all branches.

Simplest simplification: 
```js
function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
   if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
   if (pr.merged === true) return true;
   var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
   if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged') return true;
   return labelNames(pr.labels).some(...);
}
```
Still similar. Extract label normalization to a helper `labelName(label)` and use a loop... Extracting the label-scan into its own function reduces isPrBodyFrozen's CC: 1 + 2 (||) + 1 + 2 (||) + 1 (call if?) = 7 if written as:

```js
function isPrBodyFrozen(pr) {
   if (!pr || typeof pr !== 'object') return false;
   if (pr.merged === true) return true;
   var state = String(pr.state || '').toLowerCase();
   if (state === 'closed' || state === 'merged') return true;
   return hasMergeQueueLabel(pr.labels);
}
```
CC = 1+2+1+2+1 = 7 (the `return hasMergeQueueLabel` adds nothing). With full coverage CRAP=7 ≤ 8 → passes. The helper `hasMergeQueueLabel` would itself be new: 1 + for(1) + ternary(2) + if(1) = 5 ≤ 8 → fine.

Alternatively use Array.prototype.some — but the codebase... they use ES5-style for loops. Actually `.some` would reduce: 
```js
return (pr.labels || []).some(function(l) { return MERGE_QUEUE_BODY_LABELS.indexOf(...) !== -1; });
```
CC = 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1(some) + 1(callback if)... hmm nested functions counted separately. 

OK, so the review: BLOCKING finding = CI failure with root cause identified: `isPrBodyFrozen` CC too high (CRAP 12 > 8). Suggest extracting the label scan.

Now, other review findings. Let me look at correctness issues:

1. **Findings verification — does the fix actually address gh-960?** The ticket: PR body must be final before merge queue; finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms. The fix freezes body rewrite when `ai_validating` label present OR merged/closed. But wait — the live incident: PR #956 merged with Closes added at merge moment. In that lifecycle, the rework leg died; a later run finalized. Where does the finalize-step rewrite happen? Does the finalize step also call `postReworkBodyAndComment`? The freeze is only in `postTestReworkResults.js` — the rework publish path. The ticket says "the finalize step must not rewrite the body after validation arms". Is there another body-rewrite path (finalize step) that still rewrites the body post-arm? E.g., `machineMerge` or `retryMerge` or developTicketAndCreatePR finalize. Let me grep for updatePrBody / updatePullRequestBody callers.

2. **`pr.merged` shape**: github_list_prs — does the PR object include `merged` and `labels`? The GitHub REST list PRs API returns `merged` (wait — list PRs does NOT return `merged` field! GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls returns: url, id, number, state, locked, title, user, body, labels, milestone, active_lock_reason, created_at, closed_at, merged_at, merge_commit_sha, assignee, ... It does NOT include `merged`. `merged` is only on the single-PR GET response. However state='closed' covers merged PRs anyway. And listPrs('open') means closed never returned. So `pr.merged === true` check is harmless defense.

But important: does the GitHub SCM's github_list_prs return labels? Need to check the dmtools catalog — github_list_prs presumably returns the REST JSON array with labels as [{name}]. Probably yes.

Also GitLab MRs: _normalizeGitLabMr — what labels does it produce? GitLab doesn't have labels on MRs in the same way... Actually GitLab 15.x+ supports MR labels. Let me check _normalizeGitLabMr.

3. **The real gate**: freeze on `ai_validating` label. In the live incident, did the PR have `ai_validating` at the time of the finalize rewrite? The PR #956 merged 10:55Z; the rewrite happened at merge time when the merge bot had armed validation. The finalize body rewrite happened after validation armed → label present → frozen. Good. So the finalizing run was presumably a test-rework resume that published results and rewrote body at 10:55. With the freeze, when it re-runs post-arm, body rewrite is skipped. 

But wait — there's a subtle failure mode: `findTestPRForTicket` uses `scm.listPrs('open')`. Fine.

4. **Ordering in updatePullRequestBody**: `ensureClosesLine(refreshed, ticketKey)` — ensures Closes line is FIRST in the body. But the refreshed body replaces the entire PR body with `## ticketKey Result ... + bodyContent`. If bodyContent (outputs/pr_body.md) doesn't include the original PR description, this was already the pre-existing behavior. Fine.

One issue: previously the body had whatever content; now Closes is force-prepended — that changes body structure but is intended.

5. Idempotency check in ensureClosesLine: regex `\bCloses\s+#?952\b` case-insensitive — if bodyContent already contains "Closes #952" it's left as-is (possibly not first). Test asserts first when not present. OK.

6. **`pr.number` used in warn when pr could be null**: `postReworkBodyAndComment` — if pr is null, `pr && pr.number` → 'undefined' — fine, but then `scm.addComment(pr.number...)` would throw — but that's inside try. Pre-existing.
